description: Evolve molecular property prediction models for ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) endpoints critical to drug discovery. Focus on hERG cardiac toxicity, a major cause of drug candidate attrition.

problem.goal: Maximize ROC-AUC for predicting hERG channel inhibition (cardiac toxicity) from molecular structure
constraints: Must use only molecular structure as input (SMILES)
Model must be interpretable or provide feature importance
No data leakage between train/validation/test splits

optimization_strategies: Explore different molecular fingerprints (Morgan, MACCS, RDKit)
Try graph neural network approaches (if dependencies allow)
Combine multiple fingerprint types as ensemble features
Ensemble methods combining multiple base learners
Feature selection to identify predictive substructures

domain_context.background: hERG (human Ether-a-go-go Related Gene) encodes a potassium ion channel. Drug-induced hERG inhibition causes cardiac arrhythmias (QT prolongation), leading to ~40% of drug withdrawals. Predicting hERG liability early saves billions in failed drug development.
key_molecular_features: Basic nitrogen (positive charge at physiological pH)
